note: Conformance vectors for the loose-ends document. Shared, not owned: the
corpus generates the document and each consumer reads it, and every
consumer runs these cases so that two readings stay honest without one
importing the other. Same arrangement as address-vectors.json.
ci/loose_ends.py is the generator and the reference reader.
`python ci/loose_ends.py --vectors` runs this file against it.
WHAT A CASE ASSERTS. Given the item and the claims register in `given`,
a conforming reader reports the `expect` block: the item's key, whether
it is open, and its disposition. A reader that renders an unclaimed item
the same as a dismissed one fails the first case, which is the one this
Adding a case is cheap and is the right response to any item that was
read wrongly in the wild. Removing one needs a reason.

cases.name: an item nobody has judged is open, and carries no claim block
cases.why: open is the absence of a claim. A reader that invents disposition 'open' cannot tell nobody-looked from somebody-decided-nothing.

cases.name: a dismissed item is not open and keeps its reason
cases.why: the reason travels with the decision, or the next reader re-litigates it

cases.name: a carried item is claimed and still a loose end
cases.why: carried means somebody is following it, not that it is finished. It stays in the document until its subject changes.

cases.name: a claim on a different kind at the same address does not apply

stalled-thread:quaternionmedia/apothecar.why: a different finding about the same repository

cases.why: the key is kind plus address. One repository can hold several findings and dismissing one must never dismiss the rest.

cases.name: an unrecognised disposition does not silently void the item
cases.why: a typo in a disposition must leave the item open. Accepting any word would let a misspelling quietly close a finding, which is the failure mode a register of decisions can least afford.

cases.name: an address that does not round-trip is not a usable key
cases.why: `pullrequest` is not in ci/addresses.py's closed KINDS set. The item is still reported -- dropping it would hide a real finding -- but a view cannot navigate to its subject, and address_parses says so rather than leaving a dead link.
